items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: I walked into my drummer, the fellow that had been in the Army with me, George Howe.

ctx.x: We had a company, about 12, 15 people. And as the girls would make money, or they'd hear from home, why the show got smaller and smaller. And when it got down to where we had all the girls protected and it was all straightened out, well we went on home. Because we had money, you know what I mean? And so we went on back to New York, ourselves.

And I got back to New York -- now, this is where, where the really, the things start turning over now, see? I got back to New York and I walked into my drummer, the fellow that had been in the Army with me, George Howe. George Howe said, 'Sam,

Johnny Carey and Mal Frazier is looking for"-- that was the Nest -- "they're opening a new club called the Nest Club, and they're looking for somebody to take the band. And I told them that you would be in town and you had worked for Old Man Baron." And they'd been down to Old Man Baron, and Baron'd said that Sam is a good man, get him if you can, see? Said he's a conscientious kid, see? So --
